chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who prayed one rakʿah on tayammum, then a man came carrying two waterskins of water with him. He said: "He cuts off the salat (prayer), performs wudu (ablution), then builds upon one [rakʿah]."

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it to mean that if he had prayed one rakʿah and then had an occurrence that nullifies wudu (ablution), forgetfully, then at that point he performs wudu (ablution) and builds on [what he has prayed]. Had he not invalidated [his state of purity], it would not have been obligatory for him to depart [from the prayer]; rather, he would have had to continue in his salat (prayer). And it is not possible to say regarding this report what we said concerning others: that departure is only obligatory because he entered the salat (prayer) before the end of the time; because if that were so, it would not have been permissible for him to build on [what he had prayed], and he would have had to restart. So if that is so, then there is no valid interpretation for it except what we have stated.

key_terms.الِاسْتِئْنَافُ: restarting the prayer from the beginning
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: ritual wudu (ablution), whose nullification is discussed here
key_terms.تَيَمُّمٍ: dry ablution used in place of wudu (ablution) when water is unavailable
key_terms.يَبْنِي: he continues and completes the prayer based on what has already been performed
key_terms.يَقْطَعُ: he discontinues or breaks off the prayer

ai.seo_question: If someone prays with tayammum and then finds water during the salat (prayer), should he stop and perform wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling about one who begins salat (prayer) with tayammum and then water becomes available. The appended explanation by Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan states that the report is to be understood in the case where the person had invalidated wudu (ablution) forgetfully after one rakʿah, in which case he performs wudu (ablution) and resumes from what he has completed.
